claims.statement: DeepAgentRuntime builds its graph from resolved subagents, an approval snapshot, runtime tools, middleware, backend, memory, skills, and a checkpointer; it defaults to InMemorySaver and compiles tool approval interrupts from the active snapshot.

ConversationSaver serializes checkpoint/archive writes, persists the checkpoint before committed archive revisions, and waits for both writes to settle when its caller is cancelled; Talon records final replies in semantic history only after host-confirmed delivery.

The default Talon shell backend uses a fixed safe PATH and an allowlisted, scrubbed child environment, excluding loader-hijack variables and credential-indicating keys; its artifacts directory is created and enforced with mode 0700.

Before a turn, DeepAgentRuntime can refresh runtime tools and atomically replace the compiled graph; refresh failures retain the previous graph, and each invocation captures its graph in a context variable so a running turn is insulated from later replacement.

Talon retries whole graph invocations up to its configured budget with capped exponential backoff only for classified transient connection, timeout, status, parse, context-limit, or message-marker failures, while cancellation and terminal failures propagate; empty final text instead triggers bounded continuation nudges followed by a forced summary.

Cancellation recovery reads the latest graph checkpoint, repairs dangling tool calls, and appends an interruption marker; runtime shutdown refuses to close graph/checkpoint resources if background workers outlive cancellation.

Tool approval policy is a validated exact-name, immutable per-invocation snapshot backed by a bounded non-symlink regular JSON file and byte-revision compare-and-swap updates, so saved edits apply only on a later invocation.

The runtime batches resumable tool-approval interrupts, audits action names/counts rather than values, resumes aligned decisions, and caps approval rounds; cron turns and turns without an eligible approval handler auto-reject gated tools.

Detached background subagents are in-memory per-thread jobs with bounded capacity, separate task thread IDs, no recursive delegation, approval operator, or authorization handler, bounded outputs, and a one-hour timeout; their results are injected into an owner turn and acknowledged only after that turn completes.

If a host turn is superseded or cancelled before delivery, it requeues its background result IDs, while deliberately suppressed output remains acknowledged; repeated failed consumption is bounded by the background delivery counter.

Cron jobs persist an origin, parsed minute-granularity schedule, run state, and prompt; scheduler dispatch claims the next run before execution, marks outcomes, suppresses [SILENT] delivery, logs and continues after tick failures, and scopes management tools to the current origin.

Scheduled turns use a dedicated job thread and conversation lock, have a host timeout followed by interruption recovery, auto-deny approval, and run subagent delegations inline with a separate queued concurrency limit, bounded timeout, sanitized failure result, and output clamp rather than leaving detachable work for a later turn.

Focused tests exercise runtime refresh atomicity, authorization binding, environment hardening, approval behavior, retry classification, interruption recovery, background scheduling semantics, host timeout recovery and result requeueing, and cron ticker failure resilience.

The optional ContextDoctorRuntime capability reads the active graph checkpoint and reports bounded token estimates without invoking the model or changing state; TalonHost serves it through /context-doctor with a ten-second bound and generic unavailable or failure responses.

Cron claiming advances next_run_at before execution and expires runs that are beyond the until grace; the scheduler sweeps finished jobs before dispatch, retaining expired records only when an error or unresolved claim requires later retention/pruning.

The host persists a non-default `/model` selection per conversation root, passes it only on subsequent AgentRequests, and requires an operator to change it; the selection survives a new graph thread and host restart.

Selectable models are catalog-discovered only for providers credentialed in Talon's environment, exact-match validated, lazily constructed and cached; an unavailable saved selection falls back to the default model for that turn.

Talon binds the selected model in turn-local context and substitutes it through middleware rather than recompiling the graph; its summarization middleware uses the selected main model's context budget while delegated subagents retain the startup summarizer.
Background-delivery turns are unattended: the host omits approval and authorization handlers, and the runtime disables approval-operator authority for background delivery as it does for cron.
